source: a16z Podcast — Is AI a bubble? Data centers, GPUs, and the AI economy
summary: Application SaaS companies that embrace gross margin compression as a sign of AI adoption success—rather than resisting it—will be the winners; those that preserve legacy margin structures will lose.
summary_extended: Baker argues that SaaS companies must embrace gross margin compression as a necessary and positive signal of successful AI adoption, and that those who resist it to protect legacy margin structures will ultimately lose market share and relevance. He draws a direct analogy to retailers who refused to adopt Amazon's low-margin model and were subsequently disrupted, and points to Microsoft's on-premise-to-cloud transition as proof that accepting lower margins during a platform shift can still produce exceptional stock performance. Baker singles out public coding companies as negative examples — firms with profitable existing businesses that could fund a break-even AI push but have failed to compete with Cursor, suggesting incumbency and profitability are not sufficient defenses. Figma is cited as a positive example of proactively communicating margin compression as a feature of AI adoption rather than a bug, and Adobe is referenced in the context of navigating an AI transition. The investment implication is to favor SaaS companies that explicitly signal and accept gross margin compression as AI adoption accelerates, and to avoid or short those that prioritize margin preservation over competitive AI investment.
